content.title: About
content.content: Camembert is a soft French cheese with a white mold rind, made from cow’s milk. It has a delicate buttery flavor, a slightly nutty aroma, and a creamy texture. The cheese is traditionally aged for 3–4 weeks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Camembert originates from the Normandy region, where it was first produced in the early 19th century.
Traditionally the cheese is formed into small round disks about 11 cm in diameter and weighing 250 g.
The white mold Penicillium camemberti creates an edible rind that protects the soft interior from drying out.
The cheese is often served at room temperature to fully develop its aroma and texture.
In the United States and Canada the cheese is commonly called “Camembert cheese,” although the original French product has a protected geographical indication.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Camembert provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese supplies high‑quality dairy protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Camembert contains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: The mold cultures in the rind promote beneficial bacteria that may support gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: During aging part of the lactose is converted to lactic acid, making camembert generally easier to tolerate for those with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk proteins may experience reactions when consuming camembert.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Camembert contains about 24 g of fat per 100 g, so it should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The cheese can be salty; individuals limiting sodium should monitor portion size.

items.title: Mold rind
items.content: While the rind is edible, those sensitive to fungi may experience discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Camembert is served sliced at room temperature, often with bread, fruit, or nuts. It can be added to salads, casseroles, or used in sauces where it melts, giving a creamy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store camembert in its original packaging or wrapped in parchment paper in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. Consume within 1–2 weeks after opening. Let the cheese sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes before serving.
